Declare a judge acceptance policy

Source: R/policy.R
acceptance_policy.Rd

A policy turns descriptive calibration evidence into a decision. Thresholds are intentionally supplied by the caller because acceptable error depends on the task and the cost of each class of mistake.

Usage

acceptance_policy(
  min_agreement_lower,
  min_n,
  min_class_n,
  min_recall,
  max_missing_rate,
  max_pairwise_disagreement,
  min_stability_n = NULL,
  min_stability_runs = NULL,
  max_stability_missing_rate = NULL,
  required_probes = character(0),
  min_probe_n = NULL,
  max_probe_flip_rate = NULL,
  max_probe_directional_rate = NULL,
  max_probe_missing_rate = NULL,
  min_precision = NULL,
  min_human_reliability_lower = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  coefficient = NULL,
  max_abstention_rate = NULL
)

Arguments

min_agreement_lower

Minimum acceptable lower confidence bound for the selected agreement coefficient. The bound assessed is the smaller of the bootstrap conf_low and the exact conf_low_exact reported by agreement(). On a perfect sample the bootstrap interval is a zero-width point at 1 and only conf_low_exact is used, so a perfect sample is assessed on the same footing as a near-perfect one rather than reading INDETERMINATE where a single error could PASS. Comparing a two-sided interval's lower bound with the threshold is a one-sided test at level (1 + conf_level) / 2, and taking the smaller of two lower bounds makes it more conservative than that.

min_n

Minimum usable judge-human pairs.

min_class_n

Minimum human-reference support for every class.

min_recall

Minimum lower confidence bound for per-class recall. A scalar applies to all classes; a named vector applies only to named classes.

max_missing_rate

Maximum fraction of calibration rows without a usable judge-consensus pair.

max_pairwise_disagreement

Maximum upper confidence bound for mean pairwise stability disagreement. The interval assessed reads missing judgments both ways, over all n_items items (see test_retest()): its upper bound is the stability's pairwise_disagreement_worst_case_high, which counts every pair involving a missing judgment as a disagreement, and its lower bound is pairwise_disagreement_best_case_low, which gives each missing judgment the label that least disagrees with its item's other runs. Missing judgments can therefore turn this check's PASS or FAIL into INDETERMINATE but never cause either: a FAIL holds under the most favourable labels for them, so abstaining on runs that agree cannot fail a judge whose complete evidence would not. With nothing missing both bounds are the observed interval's. (The separate max_stability_missing_rate check can still FAIL on missingness itself.) Set NULL explicitly when stability is outside this policy.

min_stability_n

Minimum independent items with at least two stability judgments (n_items_scored; items counted only by the worst or best case do not count). Required when max_pairwise_disagreement is not NULL and rejected otherwise.

min_stability_runs

Minimum repeated judge runs. Required when max_pairwise_disagreement is not NULL and rejected otherwise.

max_stability_missing_rate

Maximum fraction of individual repeated judgments that may be missing. Below this rate missing judgments still count against the disagreement check: its upper bound treats each one as disagreeing with its item's other runs (see max_pairwise_disagreement), so a judge cannot pass by abstaining on the items where it is unstable, and its lower bound gives each the label that least disagrees with its item's other runs, so abstaining cannot fail a judge either. Only cells of the run matrix are counted: an item or run absent from the evidence entirely is not missing. Required when stability is in the policy and rejected otherwise.

required_probes

Bias probes that must be present and free of detected signal.

min_probe_n

Minimum scored items required for every required bias probe: the probe's n_scored, the items with a decided judgment in both conditions (see probe_bias()). It counts items, not judgments (n_judgments) or condition pairs (n_comparisons): a position probe over 30 pairs at repeats = 3 has n_comparisons = 90 but at most 30 scored items. Required when required_probes is non-empty and rejected otherwise.

max_probe_flip_rate

Maximum upper confidence bound for a required probe's flip rate. The upper bound assessed counts every unscored item (one without a usable judgment in both conditions; for the position probe this includes items lost to a within-condition tie) as a flip over all n_input items, so it can exceed the probe's own conf_high. The lower bound leaves out the n_unscored_tied items lost to a within-condition tie no answer could break, which are decided evidence rather than missing and stay out of it as they do of the scored items' conf_low, and counts every other unscored item (each has a missing judgment) as unflipped, over the remaining items (it is never above that conf_low). Missing judgments can therefore turn this check's PASS or FAIL into INDETERMINATE: a FAIL holds however the unscored items they leave would have been resolved. With repeats >= 2 a position item can stay scored with some repeats missing; when some answers for them could change its outcome (whether it is scored, whether it flips, or its direction), both bounds treat it like an unscored item with a missing judgment, except that it moves only in a direction those answers could reach. When some of them would leave it unscored, the upper bound moves it either way, while the lower bound counts it as unflipped unless they can flip it. The tie label counts as a possible answer when the probe used one, or when the probe's evidence does not record whether it did. Those items are found from the probe's per-judgment evidence (the evidence attribute of probe_position()'s result); when a scored item may have a missing repeat and that evidence is absent or does not reproduce the probe's counts, neither interval is assessed (INDETERMINATE). (The separate max_probe_missing_rate check can still FAIL on missingness itself.) Required when required_probes is non-empty and rejected otherwise.

max_probe_directional_rate

Maximum practically tolerable net directional effect, assessed against a conservative confidence interval whose upper bound counts every unscored item, and every scored position item that max_probe_flip_rate resolves, towards the worse direction it can reach, and whose lower bound resolves the unscored items that max_probe_flip_rate's lower bound completes (every one not in n_unscored_tied, and those scored position items) in the way that most cancels the observed direction (as flips the other way where their repeats can reach it, or unflipped), over the same n_input - n_unscored_tied items. Required when required_probes is non-empty and rejected otherwise.

max_probe_missing_rate

Maximum fraction of individual probe judgments that may be missing. Required when required_probes is non-empty so selective abstention cannot make a probe look clean; rejected otherwise.

min_precision

Optional minimum lower confidence bound for per-class precision, scalar or named.

min_human_reliability_lower

Optional minimum lower confidence bound for human-rater Gwet AC1 (nominal) or AC2 (weighted). When supplied, a single-rater gold set is NOT_ASSESSED, never accepted silently.

conf_level

Confidence level required across calibration, bias, and stability evidence.

coefficient

Agreement coefficient used by the policy. NULL (the default) selects the calibration's Gwet coefficient: "gwet_ac1" for an unweighted (nominal) calibration and "gwet_ac2" for a weighted (ordinal) one. When the calibration did not compute that default coefficient, the agreement check is NOT_ASSESSED with the reason, and the other checks are still assessed. A coefficient named here that the calibration did not compute is an error when the policy is assessed, never a silent NOT_ASSESSED.

max_abstention_rate

Optional maximum upper confidence bound for the judge's abstention rate: the share of items with a human reference that the judge left NA. See the "Missing labels and abstentions" section of calibrate_judge().

Value

A yourhonor_policy object.

Details

Stability and bias thresholds are grouped behind a parent gate: max_pairwise_disagreement switches the stability checks on and required_probes switches the bias checks on. The dependent thresholds must be supplied together with their gate and are rejected without it, so a policy can never carry a threshold that the assessment does not read.

A count or rate a check needs that is not a finite number (an NA missing rate, say) makes that check INDETERMINATE: unavailable evidence neither passes nor fails.

Examples

# A calibration-only policy: stability and bias are outside it.
policy <- acceptance_policy(
  min_agreement_lower = 0.6, min_n = 5, min_class_n = 2,
  min_recall = 0.6, max_missing_rate = 0.05,
  max_pairwise_disagreement = NULL
)
policy
#> 
#> ── yourhonor acceptance policy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Agreement coefficient: the calibration's Gwet coefficient (gwet_ac1 unweighted,
#> gwet_ac2 weighted).
#> Confidence level: 0.95.
#> Calibration:
#> • agreement lower >= 0.6
#> • usable items >= 5
#> • class support >= 2
#> • recall lower >= 0.6
#> • missing rate <= 0.05
#> Stability: outside the policy.
#> Bias: outside the policy.
#> Assess it with `report(calibration, policy = <this policy>)`.

# Eight items meet the count floors but are too few for the interval
# checks to pass.
cal <- calibrate_judge(support_gold, label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
                       n_boot = 200, seed = 1)
report(cal, policy = policy)$checks
#> # A tibble: 8 × 6
#>   check                        status         value op       threshold reason   
#>   <chr>                        <chr>          <dbl> <chr>        <dbl> <chr>    
#> 1 usable_items                 PASS          8      >=            5    Sample s…
#> 2 calibration_confidence_level PASS          0.95   =             0.95 Confiden…
#> 3 calibration_missing_rate     PASS          0      <=            0.05 Criterio…
#> 4 agreement_gwet_ac1           INDETERMINATE 0.0795 lower >=      0.6  Interval…
#> 5 class_support                PASS          2      >=            2    All clas…
#> 6 recall_I                     INDETERMINATE 0.0126 lower >=      0.6  Interval…
#> 7 recall_P                     INDETERMINATE 0.0126 lower >=      0.6  Interval…
#> 8 recall_C                     INDETERMINATE 0.398  lower >=      0.6  Interval…

# Switching a gate on requires its dependent thresholds; class-specific
# recall floors are a named vector.
acceptance_policy(
  min_agreement_lower = 0.6, min_n = 50, min_class_n = 10,
  min_recall = c(I = 0.5, C = 0.7), max_missing_rate = 0.05,
  max_pairwise_disagreement = 0.1, min_stability_n = 50,
  min_stability_runs = 3, max_stability_missing_rate = 0.01,
  required_probes = "verbosity", min_probe_n = 50,
  max_probe_flip_rate = 0.1, max_probe_directional_rate = 0.05,
  max_probe_missing_rate = 0.01
)
#> 
#> ── yourhonor acceptance policy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Agreement coefficient: the calibration's Gwet coefficient (gwet_ac1 unweighted,
#> gwet_ac2 weighted).
#> Confidence level: 0.95.
#> Calibration:
#> • agreement lower >= 0.6
#> • usable items >= 50
#> • class support >= 10
#> • recall (I) lower >= 0.5
#> • recall (C) lower >= 0.7
#> • missing rate <= 0.05
#> Stability:
#> • pairwise disagreement upper <= 0.1
#> • items >= 50
#> • runs >= 3
#> • missing rate <= 0.01
#> Bias (required probes: "verbosity"):
#> • scored items >= 50
#> • flip rate upper <= 0.1
#> • directional rate upper <= 0.05
#> • missing rate <= 0.01
#> Assess it with `report(calibration, policy = <this policy>)`.
